text:
erin: heads-up: I ran into a production hit where the async python client retries after a transient 502 and ends up re-sending an already-exhausted async generator body. server creates the resource twice.
sam: ouch. can you paste a tiny repro?
erin: simplified example (async generator source + streaming POST):
```py
async def long_stream():
    for i in range(10):
        await asyncio.sleep(0.5)
        yield json.dumps({
            \"seq\": i,
            \"payload\": \"...\"
        }).encode()

# consumer
async for chunk in client.files.upload_stream(long_stream(), retry=RetryConfig(max_attempts=4)):
    handle(chunk)
```
When the upstream returns a transient 502 and the client triggers the standard retry/backoff path, the retry machinery attempts to re-dispatch the same generator object. because the generator has been partially consumed, the re-send is incomplete and the server logs show duplicate side-effects (two resource rows).
julia: is the client adding any idempotency header by default? i thought we added one for write ops.
erin: only for simple body types (bytes/str). for async iterators we intentionally skip auto-idempotency because we couldn't guarantee replay semantics; but the retry code still tries to re-run the request if the exception occurs during backoff/auth refresh, which is the bug.
nate: so the invariant we want: \"we must not transparently replay non-rewindable request bodies\". we should either: (A) never attempt transparent retries for unseekable bodies, (B) require an explicit opt-in (idempotency token or buffer wrapper), or (C) buffer the whole body in-memory (dangerous for large streams).
sam: agree with (A) as default. can we provide a helper like `client.utils.rewindable(async_iter, max_buffer=1_048_576)` that buffers up to N bytes and raises if exceeded? that would let users opt into safe replay without surprising memory growth.
erin: i prototyped a shim that works: it returns an AsyncIterator that yields from a temporary buffer file if rewind is needed. small-ish streams work fine. but it's not ergonomic and not typed well. currently the function signature for upload_stream is `AsyncIterator[Text]` but we pass bytes -> typing mismatch. mypy in our internal codebase flagged this.
julia: typing fix is important. proposing we change SDK signatures to be explicit: `AsyncIterator[bytes] | AsyncIterator[str]` where we document which endpoints accept which. add a deprecation warning for older loose typing.
nate: from a runtime point of view we should: 1) add a ReplayPolicy enum to RetryConfig: {AUTO, NEVER, BUFFERED, EXPLICIT_TOKEN}. default -> NEVER for unseekable bodies. 2) add telemetry event `retry_unseekable_attempt` + `replay_buffered_used` so we can see customer impact.
sam: sample UX: `await client.files.upload_stream(stream, retry=RetryConfig(policy=ReplayPolicy.BUFFERED, buffer_limit=2_000_000))` and the SDK will buffer up to 2MB then allow retry. if limit exceeded, it will raise and surface a clear error telling users to provide an idempotency token header.
erin: also add a convenience header helper `client.headers.idempotency()` so users can call `headers = client.headers.idempotency()` and pass it through when they know the request is safe to replay.
julia: backwards-compat: we must make this non-breaking by default: current behavior *silently* retries which is bad. instead default should be conservative (no replay) and we publish a short migration guide for users. this *is* a breaking surface if we change a default, but it's safer. include release-note wording in RFC.
sam: can we also fail fast in the retry logic: if body is an async generator and request is non-idempotent, skip retry and surface the original transient error faster rather than hold client threads waiting for retry/backoff?
erin: yes, and unit tests show that skipping retry reduces duplicate resources. I added an integration test that mocks a token refresh during streaming and asserts only a single server-side resource appears.
ci-bot: ticket INF-4325 created: \"async-unseekable-replay-safety\" priority=high.
ci-bot: PR #6134 opened by erin: draft/feat/replay-policy-buffered -> adds ReplayPolicy, buffering helper, telemetry event.
nate: i'll pick up the RFC for the RetryConfig API changes and the typing migration plan. pinging @sam and @julia for review.
erin: thanks all. follow-ups: - RFC in two days - quickstart snippet for idempotency header - add e2e staging test that simulates auth refresh mid-stream
julia: also update docs/compat matrix and the Python quickstart code sample.
sam: one more ask: include a short cookbook entry showing safe patterns for large uploads (multipart+resume vs buffered replay) so users can avoid buffering big files.
erin: noted. i'll attach the small replay-proof helper and test in the PR. link to internal repro: https://stash.redwood/devex/async-replay-proof.
ci-bot: merging blocked: needs security review (large-file buffering).
